macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street ends record-setting week higher
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.6%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.8%, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.6% on Friday, leaving all three major U.S. indexes higher for the week and the S&P 500 near its record high.[1]

items.title: Rising inflation expectations pressure bonds and Fed outlook
items.summary: Preliminary University of Michigan data showed consumer sentiment falling to 46.3, while one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7% and five-to-10-year expectations reached 3.5%. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.24%, and markets continued to price the possibility of another Fed rate hike at the October 27–28 meeting.[2]

items.title: Oil remains elevated amid geopolitical uncertainty
items.summary: Brent crude remained above $100 per barrel as markets continued to assess disruptions and uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict and global energy supplies. Higher oil prices and Treasury yields remained key risks for equities.[3]

items.title: Delta Air Lines reports weaker-than-expected results
items.summary: Delta reported third-quarter earnings of $1.72 per share, below the $1.76 analyst consensus, and reduced its annual profit outlook. The stock finished little changed after recovering from an early decline.[4]

items.title: Investors turn to inflation data and bank earnings
items.summary: Markets are focused on next week’s U.S. CPI report and earnings from major banks including JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs. The data and results are expected to influence expectations for corporate profits and the Federal Reserve’s next interest-rate decision.[5]

items.title: Moderna and major technology stocks rally
items.summary: Moderna surged more than 14%, while Oracle, Amazon, Microsoft, and Tesla also advanced in Friday trading. Lumentum said its optical components were sold out through 2029, highlighting strong demand linked to AI data-center investment.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin sell-off triggers more than $1 billion in liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $80,350 on October 9, its lowest level since September 18, triggering more than $1 billion in crypto liquidations over 24 hours, reportedly the largest long-side wipeout in 90 days. [1]

items.title: Blockchain.com seeks U.S. approvals for prediction markets and derivatives
items.summary: Blockchain.com has applied to the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission for licenses that would allow it to offer prediction markets and crypto derivatives to U.S. retail and institutional customers. [1]

items.title: EU orders phaseout of non-compliant stablecoins
items.summary: The European Securities and Markets Authority said MiCA-licensed crypto firms must eliminate remaining exposure to non-compliant stablecoins by January 8, 2027, including ending related trading, custody, transfers and advice for EU clients. [1]

items.title: France advances new crypto tax measures
items.summary: France’s National Assembly Finance Committee approved proposed 2027 tax changes that would tax crypto-to-fiat-pegged-stablecoin conversions, allow realized losses to be carried forward for 10 years and impose an exit tax on certain unrealized gains. [1]

items.title: NEAR rises more than 9% and reaches top-20 status
items.summary: NEAR gained more than 9% in 24 hours to about $4.97, with a market capitalization of roughly $6.25 billion and a reported ranking near 12th among crypto assets. [5]

items.title: SEC approves leveraged Bitcoin futures ETF listing
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved a Cboe BZX rule change allowing Volatility Shares to list a 3x Bitcoin futures ETF along with five other leveraged commodity products. [3]

items.title: South Korea proposes expanded crypto reporting requirements
items.summary: South Korea plans to include crypto payments above $50,000 within a declaration regime and require exchanges to retain customers’ external-wallet addresses for six years. [2]

items.title: Ethena-linked wallet moves $27.96 million of ENA from Bybit
items.summary: A Gnosis Safe associated with Ethena withdrew approximately 117.58 million ENA, valued at about $27.96 million, from Bybit within nine hours. [3]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival launches
items.summary: Saber Interactive released the horror game Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival, with reviews also going live.

items.title: Machinarium 2 announced
items.summary: Amanita Design announced Machinarium 2 during the Triple-i Initiative presentation. The release date has not been revealed, though a Steam page is available.

items.title: Maneater 2 announced for 2027
items.summary: Tripwire Interactive and Demiurge Studios announced Maneater 2, a sequel to the 2020 shark-themed action RPG. It is planned for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC.

items.title: Civilization VII receives Earthrise expansion announcement
items.summary: Firaxis announced Earthrise, a paid expansion for Sid Meier’s Civilization VII, alongside plans for additional major content updates.

items.title: Google unveils AI game-creation platform Playground
items.summary: Google introduced Playground, an experimental browser-based platform that lets users create simple playable games through natural-language prompts and refine them conversationally.

items.title: Ubisoft expands its generative-AI organization
items.summary: Ubisoft promoted its chief diversity, inclusion, accessibility, and social-impact officer to chief AI enablement officer as the company expands its Motherbrain generative-AI initiative.

items.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer released
items.summary: A Guildford studio released Star Wars: Galactic Racer, a game developed since 2023 by a team of roughly 75 people and set during the Empire’s decline.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day arrives amid Xbox restructuring
items.summary: Gears of War: E-Day launched this week after nearly six years of development, while Xbox faces leadership changes, studio closures, and layoffs.
